validated_synthesis_themes.title: Pressure paths, confinement and the missing local-force map
validated_synthesis_themes.established_knowledge: S02 and S03 establish positive-pressure jamming in granular and nylon-fiber structures, while S01 supplies vacuum fiber/rope tunability and S18 a vacuum PVC layer-beam continuum model. This is strong evidence for the existence of architecture-dependent confinement effects (P401/P402), rather than for a universal pressure-to-stiffness relation. S15 frames laminar mechanisms only; its review excludes fiber and particle jamming and provides no independent experimental replication.
validated_synthesis_themes.comparison_across_studies: S02 expands a bladder against particles inside a fabric sleeve; S03 expands a bladder against nylon fibers bounded by rigid links. Both apply positive pressure, but particles and long fibers transmit load through different contact networks and boundaries. S18 instead compresses flat layers under vacuum through a flexible membrane and validates a continuum/slip deformation prediction in a cantilever. S03 uses segmented three-point-bending force curves, so even the measured structural observables cannot be pooled with S18 without boundary and metric conversion.
validated_synthesis_themes.important_contrasts: S03 finds pressure-sensitive transition loads and slipping-branch stiffness alongside a relatively geometry-dominated jammed branch. Thus an endpoint stiffness increase does not imply that every branch has the same pressure dependence. Vacuum versus positive pressure is a boundary-path contrast, not a contradiction. S18 experimental vacuum confinement is 60 kPa; its separate 0.1 MPa FE loading is not a measured pressure sweep. S18 is a theoretical analogue to S03, not a positive-pressure fiber precursor.
validated_synthesis_themes.mechanistic_connections: CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE: the sources connect pressure inputs to architecture-dependent confinement and then to modeled resistance/sliding constraints. This connection can motivate an MP1-R pressure-conditioned structural envelope and conventional baselines. It cannot close the intermediate pressure-to-contact map: S03 assumes effective uniform confinement, S18 assumes the threshold μp, and S22 infers normal force from resistance using a borrowed coefficient.
validated_synthesis_themes.methodological_critique: The rigid reaction wall in S03 makes outward bladder expansion mechanically meaningful; a compliant or insufficiently constrained MP1-R sleeve may instead expand, rearrange packing, or change sleeve bending resistance. S18 omits transverse normal stress and admits slip-region/end/large-slip errors. Global model agreement can therefore coexist with incorrect local contact assignment. Treating p as every interface normal force would hide exactly the geometry-dependent mechanism that MP1-R needs to characterize.
validated_synthesis_themes.mp1_relevance: The pressure-controlled tunability principle is established prior art. MP1-R can investigate its actual reaction path and conditional bending response, with source pressure, specimen pressure and local contact loading represented as distinct quantities. No source supplies transferable nylon/PVC friction or modulus values for TiNi.
validated_synthesis_themes.remaining_uncertainty: The actual fluid, chamber, sleeve compliance, packing and reaction surface are still unspecified. The effect of outward loading on wire–wire and wire–sleeve contacts may differ in sign or magnitude. L04 is the weakest causal link, and pressure-conditioned bending measurements alone will not resolve it.

validated_synthesis_themes.title: Slip-conditioned bending and interface identifiability
validated_synthesis_themes.established_knowledge: S06 validates useful steel-rope stiffness limits associated with prescribed stick/slip kinematics. S18 represents evolving jammed/sliding regions in vacuum layers, while S03 represents pressure-conditioned fiber branches through an effective-section model. S04 directly measures wire–rubber sliding resistance; S22 directly measures selected internal cable-layer resistance. These results establish different modeling and measurement capabilities, not a single complete local contact law.
validated_synthesis_themes.comparison_across_studies: S06 and S11 both examine rope bending with attention to tension suppression, making stiffness-bound comparisons conditional on rope construction and fixture. Their targets differ: S06 compares cycle slopes with analytical limits; S11 characterizes/fits pinched loops and tests absorber performance. S18 adds cross-sectional sliding-region evolution, but for flat PVC layers. V-W02 adds transformation-aware frictional cable FE under axial load. These are complementary H0b ingredients whose domains must remain visible.
validated_synthesis_themes.important_contrasts: Existence of friction is weaker than identifying local N, and neither is equivalent to identifying a dominant interface. S04 pull-out selects a wire–rubber path; S22 selectively cut cable layers select internal helical interfaces. They do not constitute a joint wire–wire/wire–sleeve partition. S06 does not implement the calibrated Coulomb/contact-pressure or cycle-evolution law sometimes attributed to it. S03 branch segmentation and S18 modeled regions do not directly image individual contacts slipping.
validated_synthesis_themes.mechanistic_connections: CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE: slip constraints alter effective load sharing and can change bending slopes, while sliding offers a conventional route to dissipation. S06 constrains attainable limits, S18/S03 offer distinct transition representations, and S04/S22 show how independent interface observables can constrain a global response fit. The combination is a reason to test conventional models before adding new constitutive terms.
validated_synthesis_themes.methodological_critique: An interface force test observes resistance approximately proportional to μN plus fixture and end losses. S22 derives N from a borrowed μ and approximate area; it therefore cannot independently validate μ, contact area and normal-force transfer. Dissection/pull-out changes packing and boundary conditions, so method existence does not guarantee valid parameters for intact bending. Likewise, fitting two unknown interface resistances to one unconstrained bending curve supplies parameters but not necessarily unique attribution.
validated_synthesis_themes.mp1_relevance: G1 remains a system-identification and experimental-design requirement. Global bending may identify an empirical envelope, but dominant-interface claims require independent constraints, selectively altered interfaces, or validated local slip/resistance observations. Pull-out is an available method, not a uniquely necessary fixture or automatic scientific contribution.
validated_synthesis_themes.remaining_uncertainty: Neither global bending nor the currently validated analogue tests partitions internal and external losses in the proposed TiNi assembly. Quantitative slip progression, curvature dependence and complete hysteresis prediction remain model-specific and untested for MP1-R.

validated_synthesis_themes.title: Structural TiNi state, hysteresis and conventional transformation-aware models
validated_synthesis_themes.established_knowledge: S05 cable/component tension with DIC and IR provides direct evidence that local NiTi transformation changes structural response in its tested domain. S13 thermal/DMA comparisons demonstrate temperature- and braid-dependent response, and S11 observes mixed-rope hysteresis and absorber behavior. S12 and V-W02 establish the existence of transformation-aware frictional numerical formulations. These facts establish material and contact precedents; they do not demonstrate active transformation or dominant loss in MP1-R bending.
validated_synthesis_themes.comparison_across_studies: S05 tests nearly isothermal hierarchical cables and components in tension, resolving local fields beyond the global curve. S11 tests mixed NiTiNOL/steel ropes in cyclic bending and dynamics, whereas S13 tests braided microfilaments using small-amplitude DMA/thermal and tensile measurements. Their material architecture, loading, temperature paths and measured losses differ. S07 and V-W02 compare numerical cable predictions with existing tension data; their use of literature experiments is not independent experimental replication.
validated_synthesis_themes.important_contrasts: S07 explicitly omits friction in smooth contact; V-W02 combines a Souza law with frictional contact. Different geometry, material laws and boundaries prevent treating their discrepancies as a controlled measurement of friction. S12 physical validation concerns steel, while the SMA response is numerical. S11/S13 authors attribute effects to material and contact mechanisms without isolating their fractions. Loss tangent, global loop area and local transformation fronts therefore answer different questions.
validated_synthesis_themes.mechanistic_connections: CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE: material state changes the deformation/force carried by wires, which can alter contact loading and slip through ordinary equilibrium and existing constitutive/contact laws. A constant modulus may fail in a transformation-active domain without requiring a novel coupling term. Conversely, friction can contribute to a loop without transformation being active. Conventional transformation-aware mechanics is a live H0b alternative to either simplistic explanation.
validated_synthesis_themes.methodological_critique: Global hysteresis is an aggregate of material, interface, sleeve and fixture effects. S05 offers stronger local material observables than global loops, but its nearly isothermal tension domain cannot be imported as a universal bending threshold or as evidence for MP1-R phase activity. S11 dynamic guide friction and S13 small-amplitude/frequency-dependent measures prevent quantitative loss pooling. Declaring either material or friction dominant from this corpus would exceed the observations.
validated_synthesis_themes.mp1_relevance: A same-lot material baseline and structural-wire temperature/strain/history are needed if material mechanism or H0a sufficiency is claimed. Transformation-sensitive characterization should match the accessible MP1-R domain rather than assume NiTi identity guarantees activity. Existing numerical material/contact formulations set a demanding conventional alternative.
validated_synthesis_themes.remaining_uncertainty: No validated source independently partitions transformation and friction in the proposed pressure-controlled bending assembly. The extent to which either contributes, and whether state-conditioned pressure effects require a term beyond an appropriate conventional model, remain unresolved.

validated_synthesis_themes.title: SMA actuation, fluid generation and experimental decomposition
validated_synthesis_themes.established_knowledge: S04 establishes thermal SMA-spring actuation that squeezes a wire–rubber arrangement and changes sliding/bending response. S09 establishes SMA-driven fluid displacement with coupled thermal/fluid/mechanical modeling. S10 provides a different onboard-pump/jamming integration precedent using ECF and vacuum stiffening. These separate precedents cover important segments of the proposed architecture without demonstrating its exact integrated performance.
validated_synthesis_themes.comparison_across_studies: S04 changes circumference mechanically; S09 uses wet SMA wires, a lever and diaphragm pump; MP1-R proposes an SMA spring driving an axial piston. The force/stroke/load and cooling environments differ. S03 supplies a controlled external pressure/bending experiment but no SMA source. Together these sources motivate separating a controlled-pressure specimen envelope from source response under a characterized load.
validated_synthesis_themes.important_contrasts: SMA actuator phase change produces mechanical action; structural TiNi wires carry bending/contact load and may occupy a different thermal/material state. S04 actuator timings are not piston pressure-rise/recovery or structural-stiffness timings. S10 positive pressure creates shape actuation while its stiffness modulation uses vacuum, and its separate no-flow calibration does not establish connected-specimen transient pressure.
validated_synthesis_themes.mechanistic_connections: CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE: Bench A isolates response to imposed specimen pressure while actuator input is held outside the attribution problem. Bench B characterizes spring temperature/force/stroke and pressure dynamics under a known load/compliance. Neither alone verifies the integrated source-to-structure transfer. Their rationale follows from complementary interventions and observables, rather than from a demonstrated absence of prior methodology.
validated_synthesis_themes.methodological_critique: A blocked-piston or no-flow pressure result is an actuator limit, not a loaded transient waveform. Pressure and stroke alone cannot uniquely identify seal loss if spring force, return bias and compliance are unknown. Heat leaking from the actuator to the wires can make nominally matched pressure trials differ mechanically. Equality of steady source pressure is therefore insufficient for an integrated comparison.
validated_synthesis_themes.mp1_relevance: Retain Bench A/B as experimental architecture; physical two-rig implementation is not uniquely required. An eventual integrated comparison must match near-specimen pressure history, structural-wire temperature, loading/curvature, geometry/preload and cycle history. The source must reach the specimen pressure–volume operating envelope. No new hardware design or response-time threshold is introduced here.
validated_synthesis_themes.remaining_uncertainty: Actual spring force/stroke/temperature dependence, seal/bias forces, working fluid, leakage/compliance, recovery and pressure transport are unmeasured. S19/S21 are quarantined and cannot supply missing dynamics. MRI remains a scope constraint and supplies no core mechanics evidence.

validated_synthesis_themes.title: Integration evidence and competing explanations
validated_synthesis_themes.established_knowledge: Pressure-conditioned structural effects, interface-specific resistance measurements, local NiTi transformation and existing material/contact formulations are established at their separate source domains. This constrains broad principle claims and supplies competing model capabilities. It does not establish a full-chain response in MP1-R or require all mechanisms to be active in its operating domain.
validated_synthesis_themes.comparison_across_studies: S03/S04 are substantial partial prior art for pressure/friction and SMA/friction/bending, respectively. S06 supplies limits rather than a complete hysteresis law; S18 supplies a conventional vacuum layer continuum; S05 supplies local material evidence; S12/V-W02 supply transformation-aware frictional numerical alternatives. S09 covers a fluid source. Their coexistence in the corpus is evidence for component precedents, not an experiment that combines them.
validated_synthesis_themes.important_contrasts: H0a-R asks whether a calibrated material-dominated explanation suffices; it is broader than constant-E substitution. H0b-R includes conventional transformation-aware material/contact/boundary mechanics and can contain physically meaningful interaction. H1 as an observed interaction and H1 as a necessary extra constitutive term are distinct tests. Pressure dependence, nonlinear hysteresis or failure of S06 outside its limits does not select H1.
validated_synthesis_themes.mechanistic_connections: CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE: a staged inference can first establish an empirical envelope, then constrain pressure transfer and interface/material contributions, then evaluate locked conventional predictions on reserved conditions. The corpus supports this order because each additional causal attribution requires observations absent from the simpler global-response tests. It does not prescribe a final research direction or adjudicate novelty.
validated_synthesis_themes.methodological_critique: A calibrated parameter absorbing unknown pressure transmission or sleeve effects can give good global fits while assigning the wrong mechanism. Conversely, a deliberately incomplete baseline can fail without any new law being necessary. Additional coupling must produce identifiable local or state-conditioned predictions beyond reasonable conventional alternatives; a better fit from extra parameters alone is not that evidence.
validated_synthesis_themes.mp1_relevance: Characterization remains meaningful even if H0b adequately describes the eventual response. Claims should scale to independently supported observables: pressure-conditioned stiffness first, interface or transformation attribution only when supported, and new-law necessity only after stronger discrimination. The synthesis therefore carries unresolved questions and conditional requirements into reconciliation rather than a final gap.
validated_synthesis_themes.remaining_uncertainty: All MP1-R-specific hypothesis adequacy judgments remain prospective. No direct full-chain overlap is identified in the validated evidence base, but the coverage cannot establish worldwide absence. The accessible transformation/contact domain and claim ambition need later adjudication, without treating uncertainty as novelty.

hypothesis_state.definition: Existing contact/friction/stick–slip and transformation-aware material/boundary models suffice without a new constitutive coupling law.

hypothesis_state.discrimination_rule: A specified adequate conventional baseline must fail beyond combined uncertainty after known alternatives are bounded; rejecting one simplification does not reject the family.

hypothesis_state.definition: Meaningful confinement/contact/material-state interaction produces response not adequately captured by declared simpler alternatives.

hypothesis_state.discrimination_rule: If separable components or an appropriate conventional model account for the state-conditioned effect within uncertainty, extra claimed interaction/necessity is unsupported in that domain.

chapter2_blueprint.prohibited_wording: S06 predicts loops; global bending proves inter-wire dominance; interface gap established.

chapter2_blueprint.subsection_title: TiNi thermomechanical response and conventional material/contact alternatives
chapter2_blueprint.scientific_purpose: Separate direct transformation evidence from loss interpretation and numerical precedent.
chapter2_blueprint.primary_claim: Local transformation matters in tested tension domains and existing models can combine it with contact.
chapter2_blueprint.comparison_required: Compare DIC/IR cable/component evidence, braid DMA, mixed-rope bending and FE.
chapter2_blueprint.contrast_required: Frictionless versus frictional models; steel experiment versus SMA simulation; losses versus fractions.
chapter2_blueprint.critical_limitation: Same-lot bending-domain activity and loss partition unmeasured.
chapter2_blueprint.connection_to_next: Distinguish structural TiNi state from the SMA source.
chapter2_blueprint.prohibited_wording: NiTi implies active transformation; conventional models disproved; new law required.

chapter2_blueprint.subsection_title: SMA actuation, fluid sources and matched structural validation
chapter2_blueprint.scientific_purpose: Explain source/component precedents and Bench A/B identifiability rationale.
chapter2_blueprint.primary_claim: SMA/friction and SMA/fluid precedents are separate; proposed source performance remains unmeasured.
chapter2_blueprint.comparison_required: Compare circumferential squeeze, wet pump and ECF integration with proposed spring/piston scope.
chapter2_blueprint.contrast_required: Actuator versus structural temperature; positive shape actuation versus vacuum stiffening.
chapter2_blueprint.critical_limitation: Dead-head/no-flow calibration and steady pressure do not validate loaded transients.
chapter2_blueprint.connection_to_next: Close with bounded competing hypotheses and unresolved questions.
chapter2_blueprint.prohibited_wording: Universal SMA cooling times; two rigs scientifically novel; unmatched response proves coupling.

chapter2_blueprint.subsection_title: Evidence-bounded competing explanations and unresolved questions
chapter2_blueprint.scientific_purpose: Prepare later adjudication while preserving hypothesis competition.
chapter2_blueprint.primary_claim: H0a/H0b remain plausible; H1 is not yet distinguishable and extra-law necessity is not established.
chapter2_blueprint.comparison_required: Connect local material/contact observations with locked baseline prediction and matched integration.
chapter2_blueprint.contrast_required: Material-only, conventional transformation-aware contact, observable interaction and new-law necessity.
chapter2_blueprint.critical_limitation: No MP1-R data; definitions and adequacy criteria must be explicit.
chapter2_blueprint.connection_to_next: Handoff to later adjudication; no final gap or contribution here.
chapter2_blueprint.prohibited_wording: H1 proven/best/winner; worldwide absence; final novelty/gap.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: First positive-pressure variable-stiffness structure or fiber-jamming principle/model.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S02/S03 establish the principle and S03 architecture-specific modeling.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Report the tested TiNi system and its observed bounds without a first claim.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: First SMA-controlled friction mechanism in wire-based flexible structures.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S04 supplies direct prior art.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Specify the interface, force path and measured behavior.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: First multi-wire slip-state beam/stiffness model or wire-jamming system.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S01/S03 and S06 preempt broad claims.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Use existing models as scoped comparators.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: First NiTi wire-jamming system established by corpus absence.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: The validated corpus does not demonstrate that global absence.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: No direct full-chain overlap identified in the validated evidence base; no worldwide absence claim.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: S18 proves positive-pressure fiber jamming or is a direct S03 precursor.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Corrected S18 is vacuum PVC layer jamming; direct lineage not established.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: P2 theoretical analogue only.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Fluid pressure directly equals every wire interface normal force.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Pressure and force have different dimensions; membrane/reaction/contact map is missing.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Measure specimen p and independently calibrate contact forces or bounds.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Higher pressure necessarily raises every bending-stiffness branch or every interface force.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S03 branch dependence and unknown outward MP1-R force path prevent generalization.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Specify geometry, branch and controlled domain.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Global bending/hysteresis proves inter-wire jamming or a dominant interface.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Multiple unobserved material/contact/sleeve/end terms; no unique attribution.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Global bending defines an envelope; add constraints for mechanism assignment.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: NiTi presence proves active transformation or transformation necessarily dominates hysteresis.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Material identity, author interpretation and unpartitioned loops are insufficient.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Use same-lot state-domain evidence; leave fractions unresolved.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Conventional models are insufficient or a new constitutive law is required.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: No appropriate locked MP1-R test; conventional material/contact formulations exist.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Necessity remains unresolved until discriminating predictions are tested.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: S06 predicts complete Coulomb hysteresis loops or local pressure transfer.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Its formulation validates stiffness limits and leaves cycle prediction open.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Distinguish measured loops from predicted bounds.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: S07 implements friction, or S12 experimentally validates NiTi shake-table behavior.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S07 contact is frictionless; S12 physical tests concern steel.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Separate numerical precedent and actual experimental material.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Wire–wire/wire–sleeve disambiguation is already a scientific knowledge gap.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Separate interface-method precedents exist; corpus demonstrates an identification requirement.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: G1: system-identification and experimental-design requirement.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Dedicated pull-out is a universal standard or uniquely necessary, and independently identifies μ and N.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Different methods exist; force-only tests constrain a product with parasitics.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Choose justified interface-specific observables; independently constrain μ/N if needed.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: S22 separates cable–sheath and internal wire friction in the same experiment or directly measures N.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: It measures selected internal-layer resistance; N and pressure are inferred.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Internal-interface resistance precedent only.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: SMA fluid generation or a spring replacing another drive is a new principle.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S09 establishes SMA-to-fluid displacement precedent.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Characterize exact source operating envelope; different implementation is not novelty.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Passive SMA cooling always exceeds 30 s, or S04 timing determines piston/stiffness timing.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S04 timings are specimen-specific; S21 quarantined; source and structural clocks differ.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Measure pressure and response rise/recovery under specified thermal/load conditions.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Bench A/B is experimentally validated for MP1-R or inherently a literature gap.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: It is a justified decomposition, not tested hardware or demonstrated absent method.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Architecture for future independent characterization and matched integration.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: No prior work combines relevant mechanisms, no unified theory exists, or search saturation is exhaustive.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Partial overlaps and conventional combinations exist; absence and exhaustive coverage not established.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Keep corpus-limited identification wording and explicit unresolved integration.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: A changed actuator response at unmatched p/T/history proves new coupled mechanics.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Thermal, transport, sleeve and history effects remain conventional explanations.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Match near-specimen trajectories and bound confounders first.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Different geometry/material/platform, more pressure levels, FEA or held-out testing alone is novelty.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Implementation and validation choices do not establish an unresolved mechanics claim.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Use these choices to test defined relations; no novelty adjudication in Phase 4.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: MRI-compatible/safe/conditional prototype or globally locked final MP1-R topic.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Scope proposal and restricted background do not validate a device or topic lock.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: MRI-oriented design constraint; MP1-R is the active scope evaluated.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: Review taxonomy or its cited result is an independent primary experiment.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: S15/S17 are secondary; S16 is E2 and cannot supply detailed mechanics.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Trace primary evidence and do not double-count review/primary results.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: S19, S20 or S21 supplies scientific support, or invalid historical identities can be restored.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Quarantine/retirement remains binding.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Exclude them from scientific source references; retain only status/provenance.

prohibited_overclaims.prohibited_claim: All hysteresis, pressure sensitivity or failure of constant E confirms H1.
prohibited_overclaims.reason: Conventional material/contact models can generate these outcomes.
prohibited_overclaims.safe_boundary: Separate coexistence, identifiable interaction and necessity of an additional law.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Which interface-neutral versus interface-specific characterization claim is defensible before geometry is confirmed?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: A scope choice for later adjudication, not a final gap.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Which actual force-path calibration or bounds can support local-contact language?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: Do not infer normal force from pressure alone.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Is material-state attribution necessary and feasible in the accessible operating domain?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: Narrow claim scope if transformation cannot be discriminated.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: What conventional baseline capability and adequacy criterion match the intended claim?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: A bounds-only model is not a full loop competitor.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Does later evidence justify studying interaction, or is the empirical characterization sufficient?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: H1-new remains an optional stronger claim, not a prerequisite for the rescope.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: What source operating-envelope and matched integration evidence are necessary for the selected scope?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: No borrowed response-time threshold or integrated success assumption.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Which unresolved questions deserve later gap evaluation, with what additional verification standard?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: Unresolved here does not mean novel, absent worldwide or a demonstrated scientific gap.

questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.question: Which cross-run interpretive differences survive a separate reconciliation?
questions_requiring_phase5_adjudication.boundary: Only a later authorized reconciliation may access another run; no winning interpretation is selected here.

stop_rule: Stop before other-run inspection/reconciliation, final gap/novelty adjudication, Chapter 2 drafting, experiment redesign or Phase 5 execution.
